correctedCritiques.pro-brute-cause-insufficient: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes a causally basic origin from a rational explanation, questioning whether brute physical proposals can satisfy the affirmative’s explanatory ambition. Principal limitation: Its underdefined sequence of first cause, last cause, teleological completion, and self-actualizing logical foundation never establishes their interrelations, while presupposing that causal sufficiency must furnish purposive intelligibility. Live burden: The affirmative must demonstrate why rational inference requires purposive termination, specify how its proposed foundation provides that requirement, and confront the possibility that a physical terminus remains causally basic without becoming explanatorily exhaustive. Locked score: The mixed band preserves burden contact and a challenge to brute explanation, counterbalanced by conceptual instability, insufficient warrant, overstatement, and incomplete engagement with the strongest alternative.
correctedCritiques.pro-logical-moments-trinity: Strongest feature: The move attempts the debate’s motion bridge, connecting an absolute self-understanding foundation to the Christian Trinity instead of concluding with necessity, mentality, or abstract theism. Principal limitation: Its transition from logical moments to distinct divine persons remains unsubstantiated, because Aquinas’s characterization and Christian nomenclature establish neither identity nor the necessity that an absolute being contains this structure. Live burden: The affirmative must define universality, particularity, and individuality, derive personal distinction from their relations, and demonstrate why that derivation corresponds uniquely to the Christian Trinity rather than presenting a metaphorical resemblance. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes exceptional motion relevance and a recoverable proposal while preserving reservations about warrant, conceptual mapping, calibration, and the missing Trinitarian bridge.
